Faculty Senate Executive Committee Report #2024-2025-12 Introduction: April 10, 2025 Faculty Senate Meeting For Approval: May 1, 2025 Proposed Revisions to Appendix C of the University Manual By-Laws of the Faculty Senate Amendments pertain to converting the Special Budget and Administration Committee to a Permanent Standing Committee (According to Section 12.1 of the By-Laws, amendments require two meetings and a two-thirds majority vote of senators present to pass.) RATIONALE: According to Article II, Section 4 of Appendix B of the University Manual (Constitution of the Faculty Senate), the Senate shall establish such standing and special committees as it deems necessary to carry out its functions.
During AY 2023-2024, the University community faced operational changes, including various administrative policy initiatives and the planned transition to a new budget model, then known as IBB.
The proposed pace of change and the sheer quantity of new initiatives strained the ability of the Faculty Senate Executive Committee (FSEC) to respond appropriately and react in a coordinated, meaningful, and timely fashion.

The FSEC concluded that creating a special committee to advise them in these and related matters would improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the Faculty Senate.
A new group, known as the Special Budget and Administration Committee (SBAC) was created in May 2024 and was designed to exist through AY 2025-2026.
The charge of the committee was generally to advise the Senate on administrative policy developments, assist in analyzing and making recommendations regarding any major operational changes emerging under the university strategic plan, and analyze the effects of the new budget model and its implementation, as well as any other specific operational expenditures relevant to faculty.
The current FSEC has found the Special Committee to be useful and effective and has noted that other faculty senates at peer institutions have permanent committees focused on budgetary matters.
The FSEC therefore recommends that the special committee now become a permanent standing committee.

MOTION: THAT THE FOLLOWING LANGUAGE BE INSERTED INTO APPENDIX C 4.90 The Budget and Administration Committee (BAC) shall comprise five faculty members, three of whom shall be faculty senators.
The chair shall serve a two-year term and will be elected by the committee following input from the faculty senate executive committee.
The Committee shall provide reports on their activities to the Faculty Senate at least annually and more often as directed by the FSEC or the Senate.

Any specific BAC proposals for action will flow from the Committee to the FSEC and then to the Senate. 4.91 Activities of the Budget and Administration Committee will include but not be limited to: the review and, if necessary, the development of measures for tracking major or incremental expenditures, with the aim of ensuring balanced support of faculty interests; requesting information on the university’s performance toward any new goals set up under the prevailing budget model and under any proposed changes to the budget model, and raising questions about the correspondence of these allocations against performance metrics (KPIs) and the university’s Strategic Plan; monitoring administrative policies with the aim of supporting academic freedom and faculty efforts.
The Committee shall make recommendations to the executive committee and the senate about formal responses to: any plans or proposals by the committees and individuals tasked with the implementation and functioning of the budget model; any positions or policy initiatives of the institutional research office, administrative policy groups, purchasing, capital projects, and similar groups as they may identify or that arise.

They may also engage in advocacy on behalf of the faculty for support of research, instruction, professional development, travel, course caps, and service time, so that faculty thrive in their work given their contractual roles.
